learningObjective: Diagnose the appearance of NaN in a Transformer forward pass using loss / activation statistics and localize the source op.

canonicalClaims.claim: In FP16 Transformer forward passes, attention scores with magnitude > ~11 make exp(x) overflow FP16 range; naive softmax then produces NaN. Standard fixes upcast the softmax to FP32 or use a safe-softmax implementation (e.g., FlashAttention) that stably subtracts the running max.
conditions: Attention scores are held in FP16 before softmax.
Softmax implementation does not do the max-subtract trick or does it in FP16.
nonImplications: Does not imply FP16 training is unusable overall; targeted fixes suffice.
Does not imply FlashAttention is the only way to safely softmax.

misconceptions.whyWrong: GradScaler manages the loss scale for backward; it does not affect forward attention scores.
FP32 max ~3.4e38; exp(28) ≈ 1.4e12, well within range.

misconceptions.claim: NaN in Transformer training is inevitably random and non-diagnosable.
misconceptions.whyWrong: NaN causes are traceable via activation statistics and per-layer hooks.

misconceptions.claim: FP64 is required to prevent softmax NaN.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FP32 softmax is standard and sufficient for stability.
